# Sr Cybersecurity Engineer — Disneyland Resort

---
**Job ID:** 10157360
**Date Posted:** Aug 19, 2026
**Date Applied:** Sep 24, 2026
**Salary Range:** $117,500–$157,500 per year — Anaheim, CA (fully on-site)
---

## Job Summary

An Operational Technology (OT) cybersecurity role protecting the ride and show control networks at the Disneyland Resort. The engineer joins a larger OT Cybersecurity team and aligns network security solutions with Disneyland's existing and incoming attraction systems, covering attractions, live shows, and transportation venues. The posting describes the role as strategic and calls out non-traditional hours and backstage work in dark spaces, elevated walkways, and industrial environments.

---

## What You'll Do

- Advocate for and uphold design standards during multidiscipline projects.
- Develop and manage scope and schedule for the team's projects across the resort.
- Partner with system engineering groups to hit project goals and deadlines on budget, and to maintain attraction reliability and availability.
- Communicate technical requirements to technical and nontechnical audiences.
- Contribute to network design architecture standards.
- Interpret, create, redline, and review technical drawings.
- Introduce scalable processes across Cybersecurity capabilities.
- Take on secondary and tertiary responsibilities as required.

### Required Qualifications
- Minimum 5 years of related working experience in network security
- Experience working on technical projects
- Flexible and adaptable to new challenges
- Able to work individually with minimal supervision and as part of a team
- Knowledge of network and system security procedures, best practices, and the implementation and analysis of network documentation and diagrams
- Able to work non-traditional hours (occasional weekends, evenings, and holidays) in non-traditional settings
- Preferred: prior experience in entertainment venues or the attractions/theme park industry, industrial automation/manufacturing controls, and leading technical projects across multiple disciplines or teams

### Education
Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related engineering field. Preferred: one or more security certifications (Security+, CySA+, CCNA Cyber Ops, AWS, GSEC, GICSP, CISSP, or similar) and project management certifications (PMP, CAPM, PMI-ACP, or equivalent).

### Benefits
A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be included, along with a full range of medical, financial, and other benefits depending on level and position offered.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Sep 24, 2026

- **Industrial controls is the strongest match:** the preferred industrial automation/manufacturing controls background is well supported by Allen Bradley PLCs, the multi-board CAN-bus control architecture, Modbus laser-sensor collection over a dedicated VLAN (ExtrusionLine Studio), and years of machine design and commissioning.
- **Network infrastructure evidence is real but not security-titled:** the record includes building network infrastructure and deploying 750+ wireless access points (Northampton Area School District, 2016–2019), server network and VLAN configuration, reverse proxy and firewall routing, domain-based application access, and the Unified Ubiquiti Network across company sites. After the Proteor acquisition Riley managed and expanded the division's IT infrastructure.
- **Risk and documentation overlap:** risk analysis and mitigations to EU and U.S. standards for ProteorPrint hardware and cloud products, GD&T, and engineering documentation/BOM control support the standards, drawing, and documentation duties.
- **Multidisciplinary leadership and attraction-adjacent work:** CTO and Lead R&D roles cover multi-discipline technical projects. Ski lift operation with motor and control safety checks is the closest theme-park-adjacent evidence.
- **Gaps:** the data does not establish 5 years of dedicated network security work, OT security frameworks (IEC 62443 or similar), security operations tooling, or any of the preferred security or project management certifications. The B.S. in Electro-Mechanical Engineering is an engineering degree but not Cybersecurity or Computer Science.

### Now — Sep 24, 2026

- No change since application (applied today).
